title: Excel: Plan Mode lets Copilot outline a step-by-step plan before it changes a workbook
notes: claim 25: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: Microsoft's Excel guidance describes plan mode together with published licensing requirements, so treating its entitlement as unpublished is misleading. The statement that the table contains the only documented controls also conflicts with Microsoft's guidance that all Copilot Chat access settings apply. The roadmap facts and the listed paths and commands are supported.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Plan Mode is a user-selected capability rather than the default editing mode.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot in Excel opens in edit mode. In editing mode, Copilot in Excel can edit your workbook directly based on your requests. Use plan mode to come up with a plan before editing your workbook
claims.fix: Keep defaultState user-opt-in and cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/get-started-with-copilot-in-excel in sources. That page also directly supports the summary's Windows, Mac and web availability.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for Excel Plan Mode itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in Excel plan mode; Copilot Excel plan mode license billing Microsoft 365. Opened Business Central Excel guidance, Copilot service description and license options. Found plan mode within broader Excel guidance, but no dedicated Learn page.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Plan Mode's licensing model and the tier that includes it are not yet published.
claims.quote: M365 Copilot (Premium) indicates that a user has a Microsoft Copilot add-on license, including priority access for Copilot in Excel. ... M365 Copilot (Basic) indicates that a user does not have the Microsoft Copilot add-on license but does have standard access to Copilot in Excel.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the unpublished-tier statements with: 'Plan mode is one of the Copilot in Excel modes. For work accounts, Microsoft's Excel FAQ lists a commercial Microsoft Copilot subscription or a Copilot Chat-eligible Microsoft 365 or Office 365 business or enterprise subscription; Basic users have standard access and Premium users have priority access.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/get-started-with-copilot-in-excel and https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel. The first page describes plan mode and directs its licensing section to that FAQ. Remove the first Open questions bullet and the unpublished-tier clause from the cost rationale.

claims.quote: Copilot Chat in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote: Available for M365 Copilot (Basic) and M365 Copilot (Premium) users.

Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel and https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/get-started-with-copilot-in-excel rather than silently resolving the differing descriptions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a review step within Copilot in Excel and does not describe a new connection, permission, identity or wider data reach.
claims.quote: Users can review how Copilot intends to complete the task, see which data or capabilities may be used, and adjust the plan as needed

claims.claim: Plan Mode reaches no new data.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Excel plan mode data access no new permissions. Read roadmap, Business Central Excel guidance, Excel FAQ, getting-started page and Copilot privacy guidance. These describe planning and existing access boundaries, not a no-new-data guarantee for Plan Mode.
claims.fix: Replace 'Plan Mode adds a review step before Copilot edits a workbook and reaches no new data' with 'Plan Mode adds a review step before Copilot edits a workbook'. Keep the risk rating as an editorial judgement rather than asserting an undocumented data-access guarantee.

claims.claim: Group Policy Management contains the analyse-content policy at User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center > Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content.
claims.quote: If you’re using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center. ... Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: UserContentDisabled set to 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the analyse-content policy.
claims.quote: Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled  2=Disabled ... [HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; summary; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyse content removes Copilot features, including the Excel experience containing Plan Mode, from Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel OneNote Outlook PowerPoint Word

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policies are also configurable through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: The privacy guidance's Copilot restriction applies to current versions of the named apps on Windows, Mac, iOS and Android.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: The regulated-customer guidance says web experiences and modern apps are controlled exclusively by Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: The web experiences and modern apps are controlled exclusively by the Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: Group Policy takes precedence over Cloud Policy for Win32 Office apps when both are in use.
claims.quote: Rich client Office applications (Win32 apps) are controlled by both Group Policy and Cloud Policy, with Group Policy taking precedence where both are in use.

claims.claim: Copilot in Excel requires connected experiences that analyse content to be enabled.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category in Office to be enabled for Copilot to work in Microsoft 365 Apps, including Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label GUID> -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"} sets the label's content-analysis restriction through Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Set-Label -Identity "8faca7b8-8d20-48a3-8ea2-0f96310a848e" -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices cannot be configured in the Microsoft Purview portal and requires PowerShell.
claims.quote: This configuration isn't available in the Microsoft Purview portal. You must use the PowerShell advanced setting BlockContentAnalysisServices with the Set-Label or New-Label cmdlet after you've connected to Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A label configured with BlockContentAnalysisServices excludes labelled content from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps, including Excel.
claims.quote: Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps ... Microsoft 365 Copilot | Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook

claims.claim: That labelled content remains available to Copilot in other scenarios, including Teams and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Copilot audit records can be searched in Microsoft Purview portal under Solutions > Audit > Search > Workloads > Copilot.
claims.quote: Select Solutions > Audit. ... In Search > Workloads, select AIApp and Copilot. Select Search. This step searches the audit log search results to only show activities related to Microsoft Copilot.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -Operations CopilotInteraction searches the unified audit log for the Copilot interaction operation.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-Operations <String[]>] ... The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: User interactions with Microsoft Copilot are audited with Operation CopilotInteraction, which supplies the operation value for the listed search.
claims.quote: Operation | Specifies the name of the activity that was audited. | For user interactions with Copilot or Cowork, this property contains CopilotInteraction.

claims.claim: AppHost Excel identifies Copilot interactions hosted within Excel.
claims.quote: Other application-specific values: Values like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, Stream, and others indicate that the interaction was performed within these applications

claims.claim: Audit searches require a role that can search audit logs, such as Audit Reader.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal with a role that can search audit logs, like Audit Reader. Other roles can also search the audit logs.

claims.claim: No separate tenant or group Plan Mode on/off control is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Plan Mode Copilot Excel separate admin switch PowerShell API; Copilot Excel plan mode admin setting Cloud Policy Graph default. Read Copilot admin settings, copilotPolicySetting, Excel FAQ and getting-started page. No separate Plan Mode switch or API was documented.

claims.claim: The controls listed above are the only documented levers governing Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool and can't be turned off independently. All admin settings for controlling access to Microsoft Copilot Chat apply.
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].note and its rendered table note with: 'No separate Plan Mode switch is documented. Microsoft describes Copilot in Excel as a Copilot Chat tool and says all admin settings controlling access to Copilot Chat apply.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-copilot-in-excel. Do not describe the existing table as an exhaustive list of controls.

claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote | Yes | Not currently available | Not currently available | Not currently available
